1.sense: The address names the Prophet ﷺ by what he is doing at that moment rather than by his office. Muzzammil is a participle from a verb meaning to bundle oneself into a garment, and the doubled middle letter makes the wrapping thorough, cloth gathered right around. The surah begins by speaking to a man at rest and then does not leave him there.

notes.t: The root z-m-l gives zamil, a travelling companion, and the load tied on the far side of a beast to balance a rider. The picture behind the word is of something bound close and carried.
The next surah opens with the same construction and a different covering word, al-muddaththir, the one wrapped over. Two surahs address the Prophet ﷺ by his garment before giving him an instruction.

links.why: the twin opening, and the command that follows it there is to rise and warn rather than to stand at night

2.sense: The command that answers the address. Qum is to get up and stand, and standing is the Qur'an's ordinary word for prayer held through the night. Al-layla is in the accusative of extent, so the night is not a time at which to stand but a stretch to stand for, and only then is a piece cut back out of it.

notes.t: The exception arrives before any amount has been fixed. A reader reaching qalilan still does not know how much of the night is meant, which is what the next two verses are for.
The night vigil is elsewhere set as an addition beyond what is due, tahajjud held with a portion of the night. Here it is put as a bare imperative.

links.why: the closing verse of this surah, which measures what was actually done and then lifts the requirement
the night standing named as tahajjud and tied to a praised station

3.sense: The little that was excepted is now given a size, and the size comes in steps. Half the night, or half with something taken off. Nisfahu stands in place of the night named in the previous verse, so the sentence is still the same instruction being narrowed rather than a new one.

notes.t: Three quantities are offered across two verses and none of them is made binding: half, less than half, more than half. The instruction is a range with a centre, not a figure.
The same fractions of the night come back at the end of the surah, this time as a report of what was being done rather than as a command.

4.sense: The third option opens upward, past the half. Then the manner is fixed, and the verbal noun after the verb doubles it for weight. Rattala is used of teeth set evenly in the jaw, each one separate and in its place, so what is asked for is spacing rather than speed.

notes.t: Tartil is the cognate accusative of the verb before it, the construction the surah uses again at verses 8 and 16. It adds no new information, only insistence on the manner already named.
Allah describes the Qur'an as sent down in measured portions to steady the heart of the Prophet ﷺ, using this same verb of Himself. The manner commanded here is the manner of the sending.
Umm Salama was asked to describe how the Prophet ﷺ recited, and she described a recitation that separated the letters, each one distinct.
notes.src: Abu Dawud and Tirmidhi, from Umm Salama

links.why: the same verb turned around, revelation itself given measure by measure

5.sense: The reason the night is being asked for. Alqa is to throw a thing down onto a surface, and the weight is announced before the thing is named. A qawl thaqil is speech with mass in it, and the night standing is preparation for carrying it.

notes.t: The sin on sanulqi puts the casting in the future. The vigil is ordered first and the load arrives after, so the training comes before the burden.
The weight is stated elsewhere by contrast: had this Qur'an been sent down on a mountain, the mountain would have been seen humbled and split apart.
Asked by al-Harith ibn Hisham how revelation came, the Prophet ﷺ said that sometimes it came like the ringing of a bell, and that this was the hardest of its forms on him.
notes.src: Bukhari, Book of the Beginning of Revelation, from Aisha

links.why: what the same words would do to a mountain

6.sense: The night hours are named as something that comes up out of the dark, the way a shoot rises. Wat' is the press of a foot on ground, so the standing done then lands with more of the person's weight in it. And the speech is straighter, since at that hour the tongue and the attention are not being pulled apart.

notes.t: Nashi'ah is from n-sh-', the root of nash'ah, a coming into being, and nashi', a youth. The hours are treated as a thing that grows rather than a slot on a clock.

The word is read two ways in the transmitted recitations, wat'an and wita'an: as the heavier tread, or as the closer agreement between what the tongue says and what the heart holds. Both readings are carried and neither displaces the other.
notes.src: wat'an and wita'an are both transmitted readings; the exegetes also differ over whether nashi'at al-layl means the night hours as such or specifically rising to prayer after sleep

notes.t: Those praised elsewhere for this are described by their sides leaving the beds, calling on their Lord in fear and hope.

links.why: the same practice described from outside, as sleeping little of the night
the night rising set against what the risers are promised

7.sense: The counterpart to the night, and the argument for it. Sabh is swimming, the long unbroken stroke of a body moving through water, and by extension any movement that does not stop to rest. The day is full of that, which is why the standing is put where it is.

notes.t: The verse gives no list of daytime duties, only the word for the motion. What is described is not a schedule but the absence of a still point in it.
The same verb carries the sun, the moon and the rest, each one swimming in an orbit. It is the Qur'an's word for continuous motion under order.

links.why: the same swimming applied to the bodies that make the day and night in the first place

8.sense: Two commands, one for the tongue and one for everything else. Batala is to cut a thing off clean, so tabattul is severing the other attachments and turning what remains in one direction. The verb is of one pattern and the verbal noun after it is of another, and the mismatch pushes the cutting further than the verb on its own would.

notes.t: From b-t-l comes the word for a palm shoot cut away from the tree that grew it and planted on its own. The root carries separation before it carries devotion.
Tabattal is a form V verb and tabtilan a form II verbal noun. The grammarians treat the pairing as deliberate: the reflexive verb says do the cutting yourself, the noun says let it be a real cutting.
The two acts are joined in the same order elsewhere, remembering the name of the Lord and then praying.

links.why: the same pair, dhikr of the name and the prayer that follows from it

9.sense: Sunrise and sunset held by one Lord. The two words are nouns of place, the point where the sun comes up and the point where it goes down, and together they cover the whole span a person can see. The declaration of oneness sits in the middle, and the command that closes the verse is to hand the matter over, since a wakil is the one appointed to act in your affair.

notes.t: The pair appears singular here, dual at 55:17 and plural at 70:40. The number shifts with what is being counted: one arc, two solstice limits, or the whole set of daily rising points across the year.
The same title is put in the mouth of Musa answering Firawn, which is the exchange this surah returns to at verses 15 and 16.

links.why: the dual form, two easts and two wests
the title used as an answer to Firawn, in the confrontation this surah cites

10.sense: The first sign in the surah that anyone is objecting. What they say is neither quoted nor answered, and the instruction is to hold steady under it. Hajr is to cut off contact, and jamil takes the grievance out of the cutting: a withdrawal with no reply attached and no complaint carried away from it.

notes.t: Hijrah comes from this root. Departure is described here as a manner before it is ever a journey.
The same adjective is used of patience itself, sabr jamil, in a surah built on the same pattern of a Prophet ﷺ told to endure speech he will not answer.

links.why: turning away described as a gracious overlooking rather than a rupture
patience given the same adjective

11.sense: The Prophet ﷺ is told to step out from between. Dharni wa is the idiom of one party taking a matter wholly into his own hands, so the accusative that follows is not a second object of the leaving but the party left to Him. The deniers are identified by their comfort rather than their argument, and the reprieve is measured with the same word that measured the night at verse 2.

notes.t: Namah with a fatha is soft living and ease; nimah with a kasra is a blessing. One vowel separates the people who are given from the people who are comfortable.
The same idiom opens the sentence against a named opponent in the following surah: leave Me and the one I created alone.
Qalilan closes verses 2, 3 and 11. The little that is kept back from the night and the little that is granted to the deniers are the same word doing opposite work.

links.why: the identical construction, followed there by an inventory of what the man was given
respite explained as something other than a favour

12.sense: What the reprieve is a reprieve from, and it is stated as inventory rather than threat. Ankal is the plural of nikl, a heavy iron shackle. Jahim is fire at the point where heat is all it is.

notes.t: From n-k-l also comes nakal, a punishment made an example of. The shackle in the word holds and warns at the same time.
Chains, collars and a blaze are listed together elsewhere as what is prepared, in the same order of restraint before burning.

links.why: the same three items set against the reward described immediately after them

13.sense: The list runs on. Ghussah is the lump that lodges in the throat and will go neither down nor up. What is put in the place of nourishment is a thing that cannot be swallowed.

notes.t: Ghassa is used of choking on a morsel and also of grief that stops the throat. The verse names the sensation rather than the substance.
The substance is named elsewhere: a growth that neither fattens nor answers hunger, and the tree of zaqqum described as the food of the sinful.

links.why: food that fails at exactly the thing food is for

14.sense: The day the rest of it is set on. Rajafa is a shudder that runs through a mass, and the mountains take it along with the ground. Then they change state altogether: a kathib is a heap of loose sand, and mahil is sand that slides out from under a foot as soon as weight goes on it.

notes.t: Al-jibal appears twice in one verse instead of being replaced by a pronoun the second time. The repetition holds the two conditions apart, mountains that shake and mountains that are no longer mountains.
The end state is given in full elsewhere: the mountains scattered as dust, leaving a level plain with no dip or rise left in it.

links.why: the same verb naming the day itself, the day the shaking one shakes
the answer given when the mountains were asked about directly

15.sense: The address turns from the Prophet ﷺ to the people who have been talking about him. He is described as a witness against them, so his presence among them is already part of the evidence. Then the sending is matched to an older one, and the audience is placed in the position Firawn held.

notes.t: Shahidan alaykum is stated as part of what the messenger is sent for, not as an office added later. Delivery and testimony are one function.
The testimony is described from the far side: on that day a witness is brought from every community, and the Prophet ﷺ is brought as a witness against these people.
The messenger sent to Firawn is Musa. The comparison is exact in structure, arsalna repeated with the same object, so the only variable left is what the audience does next.

links.why: the witnessing seen from the Day it is given on
the sending to Firawn told at length, in a surah that draws the same lesson

16.sense: The answer to the comparison, in two clauses tied by fa with nothing between them. Disobedience, then the seizure. Wabil is from wabil, a downpour of heavy rain, so the grip is described by weight coming down rather than by force applied from the side.

notes.t: The same root gives wabal, the bad consequence a thing leaves behind. Rain, weight and aftermath sit in one word.
Wabil elsewhere describes the heavy rain that makes a garden on high ground yield twice its crop. The word itself is neutral; the verse supplies which way the weight falls.
The episode is put in the same two-clause shape elsewhere: they disobeyed the messenger of their Lord, so He seized them with a mounting grip.

links.why: the same sentence made general, disobedience and seizure across several nations

17.sense: A question with no answer expected of it. Ittaqa is to put something between yourself and harm, so the question is asking what cover would be left. The day is given a single property and no other description: it turns children grey, which is terror doing in a moment what decades do.

notes.t: Taqwa is a shield word, from wiqayah, a covering set against harm. The verse uses the verb and then names a day with nothing to set against it.
The exegetes read shiban either as an actual whitening on that day or as an Arabic idiom for hardship so severe it ages whoever meets it. Both readings are old and the choice is not settled.
notes.src: the literal and idiomatic senses are both recorded in the early tafsir; no agreement was reached

notes.t: The same day is described by another impossibility of that kind, every nursing mother forgetting the child she is nursing.

links.why: the day described by what it undoes in people rather than by what happens to the sky

18.sense: The sky takes the same day and gives way under it. Munfatir is the seventh form, a splitting that happens to a thing along its own seam rather than a breaking applied from outside. Then the promise is reported in the past tense although the event has not come, so what is guaranteed is spoken of as finished.

notes.t: Samaa is feminine and munfatirun is masculine. The grammarians offer several accounts of the mismatch, among them that samaa is being treated as a thing that has a rift in it rather than as the subject of the splitting, and they do not settle on one.
notes.src: a standing disagreement among the grammarians of the tafsir tradition over the gender of munfatir

notes.t: The same root opens Al-Infitar, where the sky splitting is the first of four clauses describing that day.
Kana with a future event is the Qur'an's way of putting certainty into tense. The phrase wa kana wadan mafulan is used the same way of a promise not yet due.

links.why: the same verb given a whole surah to open
the promise of the Lord called something that must be carried out, said by those who believed

19.sense: The passage closes by naming itself. Tadhkirah is a reminder, a thing that returns to a person what he already had rather than adding something new. The choice is then set in one clause, and only one destination is offered for the road.

notes.t: Ittakhadha is the verb of deliberate acquiring, and it is the same verb used at verse 9 for taking Allah as a trustee. The surah asks for that act twice, once of the Prophet ﷺ and once of anyone reading.
The verse appears word for word at the close of Al-Insan, after a long description of the reward. The identical sentence does different work in each place.

links.why: the same verse standing at the end of a different argument
the same construction with a place of return in place of a way

20.sense: The command of verse 2 is taken back, and the taking back begins with a description of what was actually being done. Standing near two thirds of the night, or half, or a third, and not the Prophet ﷺ alone but a group with him. The reason given for the relief is not that the vigil was wrong but that the night is not countable, since it is Allah who measures night and day. What replaces the fixed portion is whatever is easy, and around it the prayer, the zakat, a good loan and seeking forgiveness.

notes.t: Nineteen short verses on one rhyme, then a verse longer than any three of them together. The shape of the surah changes at the point where its obligation does.

Asked about the night prayer, Aisha pointed to the opening of this surah, said that the standing of the night was made obligatory by it and that they stood for about a year until the end of the surah came down, and that the night prayer became voluntary after having been an obligation.
notes.src: Muslim, Book of the Prayer of Travellers, from Sad ibn Hisham, who asked Aisha about the night prayer

notes.t: The closing promise is given elsewhere in almost the same words, whatever good you send ahead for yourselves you will find with Allah.

The mention of fighting in the way of Allah and of the zakat has led some exegetes to treat this verse, or part of it, as revealed at Medina while the rest of the surah is Meccan. Others keep the whole surah together and read the fighting as anticipatory. The question is not settled.
notes.src: the Meccan or Medinan placement of this verse is disputed in the tafsir literature

links.why: the good loan put as a question, and what is said about how it is repaid
the same idiom for travel, striking out in the land, and the concession attached to it there
